headline: Highest risk is data leakage from gpt-researcher’s broad networked research workflow into a non-networked RisingWave pair; prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content via browsers, APIs, and files, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could consume its outputs. No shared channel is documented, but the pair has a plausible content-to-input bridge through files or copied reports, so injection is possible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher exports a report that RisingWave later parses as instructions or SQL-like text
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is used between the two agents
mitigations: Require a human review step before RisingWave consumes any gpt-researcher output.
Strip executable markup and prompt-like text from exported reports.
Use separate directories for raw research output and downstream ingestion.
Add a schema validator for any text passed from A to B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad egress to third-party APIs; RisingWave has no egress, so the main leakage path is A sending sensitive workspace data outward. The pair is not proven to share storage, but if they do, A can exfiltrate more than B can.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing local documents or research reports
IF gpt-researcher is configured to send those artifacts to OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, Gemini, or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace.
Disable or scope external API keys for non-sensitive runs.
Use a separate export folder for gpt-researcher outputs.
Review outbound destinations before each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; RisingWave is a database/stream-processing system but its write or lock behavior is not documented here. Because overlapping write surfaces are not shown, conflict is plausible only under unusual shared-resource setup, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or database
IF RisingWave is configured with writable state that gpt-researcher also modifies
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same database or git checkout.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and RisingWave could ingest those outputs as downstream data. There is no documented verification step between them, so errors or hallucinated citations from A can propagate into B’s processing or decisions, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF RisingWave consumes gpt-researcher reports without validation
IF downstream jobs treat A’s citations or facts as authoritative
mitigations: Require source verification before ingestion.
Compare A’s claims against original sources.
Reject outputs lacking structured citations.
Add a manual approval gate for downstream use.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking or provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents and may send content to external APIs, while RisingWave is documented as non-networked. The main compliance issue is a potential residency or retention mismatch for data that A exports; B is not cited for a conflicting residency regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs or outputs
IF external API processing is enabled for that data
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research runs.
Rotate or restrict API keys for compliant environments.
Document retention for exported reports.
Use redaction before external calls.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing and retention controls.
